note:

title: New Zealand has a larger share of adults in the labour force
note:
Sources: Stats NZ HLFS, September 2026; ABS Labour Force Table 1, September 2026. Seasonally adjusted, age 15+.

title: Unemployment captures only part of unused labour capacity
note:
Source: Stats NZ September 2026 HLFS. Underutilisation includes unemployed, underemployed and potential labour force.
The underutilisation denominator is the extended labour force; the unemployment denominator is the labour force.

title: Party votes and seats differ because of overhangs
x_axis: Share of valid party votes / parliamentary seats (%)
note:
Source: Electoral Commission preliminary results, 7 November 2026. 131 seats, including 11 above the usual 120.
Percentages calculated from exact counts; special votes excluded. Official results due 27 November.

title: The incumbent bloc has 67 of 131 preliminary seats
x_axis: Parliamentary seats (66 for an absolute majority)
note:
Source: Electoral Commission preliminary results. TPM = Te Pati Maori. Groups are arithmetic examples, not negotiated agreements.
Special votes can change party entitlements, electorate winners, total seats and the majority threshold.

title: National has no list seats in the preliminary allocation
note:
Source: Electoral Commission preliminary results. Losing an electorate does not by itself exclude a candidate from Parliament.
A list candidate needs room in the party entitlement after electorate MPs have been included.

title: Coalition choices sit inside a constrained fiscal outlook
note:
Source: NZ Treasury PREFU September 2026, Fiscal Time Series. Open markers are forecasts; filled markers actual/unaudited actual.
Core Crown tax revenue excludes other revenue: the distance between these lines is not the operating balance.

title: The operating-balance improvement is largely a forecast
note: Source: NZ Treasury PREFU September 2026, Fiscal Time Series. Forecasts are conditional Treasury projections, not realised savings.

title: A longer view changes the growth comparison
note: Sources: Stats NZ June 2026 GDP CSV; ABS June 2026 Table 1. Real, seasonally adjusted expenditure GDP. Growth indices do not establish which country has a higher income level.

title: Today's unemployment rise in historical perspective
note:
Sources: Stats NZ HLFS and ABS Labour Force, September 2026 vintages. Seasonally adjusted; Australia quarterly monthly-rate average.
Survey redesigns affect long-run comparability; see the release methodology before interpreting small differences.

title: Slower inflation has not reversed the increase in living costs
note:
Source: Stats NZ September 2026 Household Living-costs Price Indexes. These household cost baskets include interest payments.
They differ from the CPI; the lines measure prices, not disposable income or affordability.

title: Two electorate flips alone would not reverse the majority
note:
Source: Electoral Commission preliminary results; mechanical scenario with fixed party-vote entitlements and National-to-Labour flips.
Labour substitutes electorate MPs for list MPs; National loses overhang seats. This is not a special-vote forecast.

title: Which National leads are smallest relative to specials?
x_axis: Labour minus National special-vote share needed to tie (percentage points)
note:
Source: Electoral Commission 2026 preliminary counts and 2023 candidate-vote turnout table; own scenarios.
Dots: historical-pattern benchmark. Lines: 0.5 to 1.5 times that volume, not confidence intervals.
Six lowest hurdles among nine smallest National leads. No boundary/rule adjustment; recount changes excluded.

title: How close National contests depend on special-vote volume
x_axis: Valid special candidate votes remaining in that electorate (scenario)
y_axis: Labour minus National share needed to tie (percentage points)
note:
Source: Electoral Commission preliminary candidate margins; own break-even calculation: 100 x margin / valid specials.
Each curve uses a range of possible volumes, not an official local count or a probability forecast.
Votes for other candidates do not transfer to Labour or National in NZ electorate voting.

title: National could also gain seats on special votes
x_axis: Trailing candidate minus leader special-vote share needed to tie (percentage points)
y_axis: Electorate, current leader and preliminary margin
note:
Source: Electoral Commission preliminary counts and 2023 turnout table; own historical-pattern volume benchmark.
National-Labour marginals within 2,200 votes. These are hurdles, not forecasts; smaller does not mean more likely.
Unadjusted predecessor electorates: Kapiti uses Otaki; Hutt South boundaries changed. Final party votes also matter.

title: The ranking depends on how many specials each seat has
x_axis: Labour minus National special-vote share needed to tie (percentage points)
note:
Source: Electoral Commission preliminary counts and official 2023 valid-candidate-vote turnout table; own benchmarks.
Both methods use the same national 2026 specials estimate. Neither is an official electorate-level estimate or a forecast.
Historical relative volumes may change with boundaries, enrolment rules, overseas voting and candidate-vote eligibility.
